newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher, further gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher, further gains seen.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Wednesday on tightening liquidity and dealers said they expected further rises on Thursday.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.473 percent against Tuesday's 5.430 close, with 30-day commercial paper rising to 5.35 against 5.25.
Liquidity would remain tight in the banking system in the near term, but dealers said the central bank's loose monetary policy would prevent sharp gains, dealers said.
The central bank has said it wanted the short-term interest rates to stay at around 5.00-5.50 percent.

The bond market was quiet in the afternoon as investors switched their focus to the bullish stock market, which surged 144.41 points or 2.10 percent higher to close at 7,019.43 points on Wednesday, the highest since 7,051.49 recorded on January 5, 1995.
The 10-year 86/4 government bond yield was traded at 6.1475 earlier.
